name: MiniMax-H3 Reference
summary: For PCs with 64 GB of RAM or more: the official full-precision route through diffusers. On 16 GB of VRAM and 32 GB of RAM use MiniMax-H3 (ComfyUI) instead. The same MiniMax-H3 with its reference checkpoint: up to 9 pictures, 3 videos and 3 recordings, in the order you arrange them, steer who and what appears, how it moves and what it sounds like. Needs its own 144 GB download (the text encoder is not shared with MiniMax-H3 text/frames) and, like it, far more system RAM than a 32 GB PC has unless it runs 4-bit.
vram_note: Estimate, not measured. Same plan as MiniMax-H3: the transformer is streamed, the decoders stay on the card. References are encoded at their own resolution, so many pictures or a long video add to the activations.

native.note: H3 is trained on a 768 pixel short edge at 24 fps. Width and height are multiples of 32 and frames are 17n+5 (124 = 5 s, 243 = 10 s, 362 = 15 s). Smaller sizes are much faster: 960×544 runs about 2.3× faster per step than 1344×768.

unlock.note: The diffusers docs: 5 to 15 seconds at 24 fps, short edge 768. 2K output needs MiniMax's hosted Regenerate-2K module, which is not open source.

memory.notes: H3 has a 33B transformer (66 GB in bf16) and a 32B Qwen3-VL text encoder (67 GB). Reel reads the prompt with the text encoder first and frees it, then runs the transformer with its blocks streamed through the GPU. The diffusers docs put the host RAM need at about 75 GB with 8-bit weights; with 32 GB of RAM the two parts are loaded one after the other (slower: the transformer is read again for every clip) and 4-bit weights are the only way to fit. The model is guidance-distilled, so there is no guidance or negative prompt.

references.label: References
references.help: Pictures (people, places, objects), videos (motion, shots) and recordings (voices, music). Their order matters: call them <Picture 1>, <Video 1>, <Audio 1> in the prompt.

match_audio.label: Make the clip as long as the first recording
